Penn State's art museum in a striking 73,000-sq-ft Allied Works building that opened June 1, 2024 at the edge of the Arboretum, nearly doubling exhibition space to 20 galleries with a store, cafe and sculpture path. Free admission; a genuine regional cultural destination.
https://creamery.psu.edu/

The symbolic heart of Penn State, crowning the hill above the campus mall. The 1930 Georgian building sits on the site of the original 1859 College Building of the Farmers' High School and houses the Land-Grant Frescoes by Henry Varnum Poor. Grounds open daily; the lawn is the campus's ceremonial gathering place.
ph: Photo: PSUMark2006 · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.w: One of the most photographed landmarks in Pennsylvania: a crouching mountain lion carved by sculptor Heinz Warneke from a 13-ton block of Indiana limestone, given by the Class of 1940. Reopened to visitors after a 2021-2022 site renovation; free, open-air, always accessible.

rows.n: Beaver Stadium & Penn State All-Sports Museum
rows.w: The 106,000-seat home of Penn State football and its All-Sports Museum, whose Upper and Lower galleries trace over a century of Nittany Lion athletics. Museum open Tue-Sat 10-4, Sun 12-4 (reduced winter hours; home-game-week changes); staff take guests to the club level for a view inside the bowl. Note: the stadium itself is under a multi-year renovation (Project Surge) through 2027.

rows.n: The Arboretum at Penn State (H.O. Smith Botanic Gardens)
rows.w: 370 acres of gardens, meadows and woodland walks a mile west of Beaver Stadium, centered on the 10-acre H.O. Smith Botanic Gardens with pollinator habitats, water features, an Overlook Pavilion and a children's garden. Free admission, open dawn to dusk daily.

A remarkably intact Victorian county-seat downtown along Spring Creek, listed on the National Register, built during a 19th-century iron-and-industry boom and once home to seven Pennsylvania governors. Grand houses, the 1889 railroad station and a walkable core of shops and eateries. Free, self-guided.
ph: Photo: Pubdog · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.n: Boalsburg Historic District (Birthplace of Memorial Day)
rows.w: A walkable stone-and-clapboard village that claims the first Memorial Day observance, traced to an 1864 cemetery gathering; the town center is full of shops, cafes and 18th-19th-century buildings and celebrates with a large Memorial Day weekend of events. Free, self-guided.

The estate of the Boal family since 1789, whose Columbus Chapel — brought from Spain in 1909 by a Columbus descendant who married into the family — holds the explorer's admiral's desk, two relics of the True Cross and centuries of European art. Guided 90-minute tours Wed-Sun at 2pm; other times by appointment.

The mountain that gives Happy Valley its identity, with 8 miles of trails and seven overlooks above the valley. The short climb to the Mike Lynch Overlook (marker #3, ~0.6 mi up) gives the classic view over State College and campus; the full loop is ~4.8 mi. Limited trailhead parking in Lemont; free.

A National Register grist mill (1786/1894) on Spring Creek in Bellefonte's waterfront district, extensively restored and reopened in 2021 as a boutique hotel, restaurant and cocktail bar. A landmark on the Riverwalk; dine or stay to see the interior.

The restored ironmaster's mansion of Centre Furnace — the 18th-century iron works whose owners helped found Penn State — now the home of the Centre County Historical Society and listed on the National Register. Furnished to the Moses Thompson era (1842-1891). Guided tours on posted days; grounds and gardens open.

America's only all-water cavern, toured entirely by boat, plus a wildlife park with a bus safari and off-road mountain tours. Cavern tours run Feb-Dec (daily 9-4 hourly in summer); the farm-nature-wildlife park runs Apr 1-Nov (closed for winter through Mar 31). Paid admission; the cave boat tour is not wheelchair accessible.
ph: inside Penn's Cave (cave interior is the place)
Photo: VitaleBaby · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.w: A 3,394-acre park atop the Allegheny Plateau built around a 250-acre lake and one of the state's finest bogs (1,992-acre Natural Area) with orchids and carnivorous plants. The half-mile boardwalk Bog Trail is the signature walk; 20 miles of trails, swimming and boating. Free day use; open year-round.
ph: Photo: Ruhrfisch · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.w: A 62-acre nature center less than two miles from campus, pairing a historic farmstead with a 50-acre limestone-fed wetland crossed by a boardwalk. Run by Centre Region Parks & Recreation; grounds free and open daily, with programs and a visitor barn. Good for families and birders.

The valley's four-season recreation hill: 14 ski/snowboard trails in winter and a summer Fun Centre with go-karts, mini-golf, batting cages, a skate park and driving range, plus an outdoor amphitheater for concerts. Paid activities; hours are seasonal.

Historic lakeside park, home to Leap-the-Dips (1902) — the world's oldest operating wooden roller coaster and a National Historic Landmark. Note: all rides have stayed closed since 2024 (declining attendance and insurance costs); for 2026 the park runs mini-golf, batting cages, courts, yard games and live-music events with free grounds admission.

The headquarters of the American Philatelic Society, the world's largest nonprofit stamp-collectors' organization, in the restored 1900 Pennsylvania Match Factory. Highlights include a fully reconstructed century-old general store and post office, a library and galleries. Open to visitors; check hours.

Pennsylvania's museum of the citizen-soldier, set on the 28th Division Shrine grounds in Boalsburg. CLOSED to the public since Dec 8, 2024 for a $3.4M modernization (HVAC, geothermal, preservation systems); the reopening, once slated for Feb 2026, has slipped to 2027. The outdoor grounds and memorials remain worth a look; galleries are shut.

1854 engineering marvel: a three-track loop that let locomotives climb the Alleghenies for the first time, still an active Norfolk Southern main line with a train passing roughly every half hour. Funicular (when running) or 194 steps up to the trackside viewing area; small museum and gift shop. Designated a National Historic Landmark in 1966.

Three floors in the Pennsylvania Railroad's 1882 Master Mechanics Building telling the story of the men and women of 'Railroad City,' plus the Harry Bennett Memorial Roundhouse with a working 105-ft turntable and rolling stock. Also the ticketing gateway for Horseshoe Curve.

Depression-era Altoona candy maker founded by brothers Bill and Bob Boyer, who invented the Mallo Cup in 1936 — the first cup candy in America, still made downtown along with Smoothie peanut-butter cups. Factory outlet store on-site with the collectible 'Mallo Cup points.'
